literal: Ocean-like desire even though suffering, palmyra-horse not mounting, than woman, greatly worthy thing there is not.
translation: There is nothing more greatly worthy than a woman who, even though suffering from a desire as vast as the ocean, does not mount the palmyra-horse.
modern: கடல் போன்ற காம நோயால் துன்புற்றாலும், மடலேறாத பெண்ணை விடப் பெருமைக்குரியவர் வேறு யாரும் இல்லை.
explanation: In classical Tamil love poetry, a man suffering from intense, unrequited love may threaten to ride a 'maḍal' (a painful horse made of rough palmyra stems) to publicly declare his grief. However, women are expected to maintain their modesty and never resort to this extreme public act. This couplet praises the restraint of women, stating that there is nothing more noble or worthy of respect than a woman who bears a desire as vast as the ocean without ever resorting to mounting the palmyra-horse. Her self-control and adherence to modesty, even under immense emotional suffering, represent the pinnacle of dignity.
